sessionTitle: Latest Cobalt VMs and Azure Boost enhancements​

announcements.name: Cobalt 200 unveiled
announcements.shortDescription: Azure's next Microsoft-designed Arm CPU, delivering up to 50% higher performance over Cobalt 100 and positioned as Azure's leading performance offering.
announcements.longDescription: Cobalt 200 is Azure's next Microsoft-designed Arm CPU and the most exciting item on the Cobalt roadmap, following the strong customer reception of Cobalt 100. It is positioned as Azure's leading performance offering, with a new VM family taking shape around it. Cobalt is described as Azure's all-silicon CPU purpose-built for the cloud, reshaping the price-performance conversation; Cobalt 100 delivered up to 2x the .NET performance of the prior generation and up to 20% lower cost than comparable Azure VMs.

announcements.name: New Cobalt 200 VM families
announcements.shortDescription: A high-memory MP series (16 GB/vCPU, up to 1.3 TB) and a dense local-storage LP series (up to 23 TB NVMe local storage) join the refreshed DP, DPL, and EP families.
announcements.longDescription: Cobalt 200 introduces entirely new VM types built in response to customer requests, alongside refreshed existing families. The new high-memory MP series sets a ratio of 16 GB of memory per vCPU, scaling up to 84 vCPUs and 1.3 TB of memory in a single VM, targeting large in-memory databases, caches, big analytics, relational databases, and ERP. A new dense local-storage LP series offers 8 GB memory per vCPU, up to 128 vCPUs, 1 TB of memory, and up to 23 TB of NVMe local storage for data preprocessing, storage caching, databases, big data analytics, and search/index engines.

announcements.name: Cobalt 200 regional launch
announcements.shortDescription: Launching in West US 3, East US 2, Central US, and Sweden Central, with more regions to follow.
announcements.longDescription: Cobalt 200 is launching in West US 3, East US 2, Central US, and Sweden Central, with region expansion to continue from there. The product availability region link referenced on the slide is the source of truth for the latest regional footprint. Arm-based VMs are built into Azure the same way x86 VMs are, using the same control plane, tools, and workflows (portal, CLI, marketplace, scale sets, monitor, backup, AKS).

announcements.name: Next-generation Azure Boost GA
announcements.shortDescription: Generally available with the first VMs (Intel-based V7), delivering up to 400 Gbps networking bandwidth and 1 million remote-storage IOPS.
announcements.longDescription: Niko Pamboukas introduces the latest generation of Azure Boost, Azure's server offload technology, which has recently become generally available with the first VMs using it—the Intel-based V7 VMs. Azure Boost is a Microsoft-designed system that offloads virtualization tasks traditionally handled by the hypervisor and host OS onto specialized hardware and software, improving performance, host isolation, servicing, networking, and storage access. Relative to Build 2025, the next generation delivers dramatic increases in storage throughput and IOPS, plus a deep-dive feature, Guest RDMA, for direct memory-to-memory transfers between VMs.

announcements.name: Guest RDMA on Azure Boost
announcements.shortDescription: Limited preview kicking off June 2026, enabling direct memory-to-memory transfers between VMs via the Microsoft Azure Network Adapter.
announcements.longDescription: Guest RDMA on Azure Boost enables direct memory-to-memory data transfers between VMs, demonstrated on a distributed AI inference workload using a prefill VM and a decode VM. Comparing RDMA versus TCP transport on the same model, prompts, and VMs, RDMA showed up to 2.2x higher throughput, a 3x reduction in time to first token, and roughly 20-25% faster token generation. The preview program kicks off in June 2026 as a limited preview to work closely with early customers, with a sign-up form available to join.

announcements.name: Intel DSv7/ESv7 GA
announcements.shortDescription: Built on Intel Xeon 6 Granite Rapids with up to 15% CPU gains, scaling to 372 vCPUs and 2.8 TB memory.
announcements.longDescription: The Intel DSv7 and ESv7 series VMs are now generally available and are the first VMs to bring the latest generation of Azure Boost performance to customers. They are based on Intel's sixth-generation Xeon 6 Granite Rapids processor, delivering up to 15% CPU performance improvement over the prior generation, scaling up to 372 vCPUs and 2.8 TB of memory with turbo frequency up to 4.2 GHz. Running on Azure Boost servers, they reach up to 400 Gbps networking bandwidth, up to 800K IOPS and 20 GB/s throughput to premium V2/ultra remote storage, and up to 9.6 million IOPS and 53 GB/s throughput to local NVMe temp disk.

announcements.name: AMD DA/EA/FAv7 VMs
announcements.shortDescription: Powered by 5th-gen AMD EPYC Turin, up to 35% CPU improvement, in 11 regions with broader expansion in 2026.
announcements.longDescription: Azure's AMD-based DA, EA, and FAv7 VMs cover general purpose, memory optimized, and compute optimized workloads, with options for local SSD and new constrained-core sizes for better cost control. They are powered by fifth-generation AMD EPYC Turin processors, delivering up to 35% CPU performance improvement over the prior generation, scaling up to 160 vCPUs and 1.25 TB of memory with boost frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The VMs already live in 11 regions with broader expansion planned in 2026, and show gains including up to 25% for Java, 65% for in-memory caching, 80% for crypto, and 130% on web applications.

announcements.name: Azure Integrated HSM GA
announcements.shortDescription: A first-party security ASIC acting as a local key vault meeting FIPS 140-3 Level 3, keeping keys inside the HSM boundary.
announcements.longDescription: Azure Integrated HSM (AI HSM) is Microsoft's first-party security ASIC that acts as a secure, hardware-backed local key vault, letting customers offload keys typically stored in Azure Key Vault, Azure Managed HSM, or an external key manager. Customer keys are never exposed in the clear and remain inside the AI HSM boundary while in use, without performance penalties, and the devices carry FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certification. Crypto operations are offloaded to a local PCIe SR-IOV device on the node, reducing exposure to memory-based attacks (such as crash dumps or memory inspection) while lowering latency for cryptographic operations.

announcements.name: Confidential VM live migration
announcements.shortDescription: Coming to Intel TDX, providing near-zero downtime for maintenance on confidential VMs.
announcements.longDescription: Confidential VM live migration is coming soon to Intel TDX with v6 confidential VMs, providing near-zero downtime for maintenance and upgrades. It eliminates outages and operational disruptions for mission-critical workloads while improving reliability and performance by transparently moving workloads away from failures and rebalancing capacity without customer intervention. A demonstration showed a confidential VM (CVM) migrating from a source to a destination server, with attestation and key exchange occurring and only a short blackout time before the workload resumed.
